accept: pulmonary hypertension with a loud pulmonary component

findings: Right axis deviation with right ventricular hypertrophy

echoTasks.find: Flattened interventricular septum giving a D shaped left ventricle in short axis
Dense tricuspid jet with a dilated right atrium and ventricle
Dilated inferior vena cava with reduced collapse on sniff

auscultation.added: Right sided fourth sound with a palpable right ventricular heave
auscultation.murmur: Pansystolic murmur of functional tricuspid regurgitation at the left lower sternal edge

exam.general: Middle aged woman, breathless on mild exertion, mild central cyanosis on effort
exam.jvp: Raised 6 cm with prominent v waves
exam.other: Right ventricular heave, tender liver edge, mild ankle oedema
exam.precordium: Sustained left parasternal heave, apex beat difficult to localise

history.a: Progressive breathlessness for a year, now NYHA class III, no wheeze
No chest pain, one near faint on climbing stairs last month
No clots in legs, no prior DVT, no long travel
Connective tissue screen pending, no known lung disease
Hypothyroid on thyroxine, no other drugs
Homemaker, biomass fuel exposure for 20 years

keyPoints: Refer to a pulmonary hypertension centre for right heart catheterisation to confirm the diagnosis
Order CT pulmonary angiography plus lung function and overnight oximetry to find the cause
Avoid routine calcium channel blockers without vasoreactivity testing at the referral centre
Start supervised exercise and vaccinate against influenza and pneumococcus while awaiting review
Counsel about pregnancy risk and anaesthesia risk, both markedly raised in pulmonary hypertension
management.model: Referral for invasive confirmation with cause seeking workup, supportive care, and risk counselling

sources: ESC guideline on pulmonary hypertension, in own words
ASE guidance on echocardiographic assessment of pulmonary hypertension, in own words
stem: A 47 year old homemaker from Indore reports a year of progressive breathlessness with one near faint on stairs. The second heart sound is loud with a right ventricular heave.
teaching: A loud pulmonary second sound with a parasternal heave is the bedside entry to pulmonary hypertension
Intermediate means velocity 2.9 to 3.4 m per s, and it mandates catheter confirmation
Septal flattening with a D shaped ventricle shows pressure overload in systole
Never start targeted therapy on echo alone; refer for right heart catheterisation
title: Intermediate probability pulmonary hypertension
